chunks: Habib narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Yasar, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

“A grave-robber was seized in the time of Mu'awiyah, and he said to his companions, ‘What do you think?’ They said, ‘We shall punish him and then let him go free.’ A man from the people said, ‘This is not how Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام acted.’ They said, ‘And what did he do?’ He said, ‘He said: The grave-robber’s hand is cut off,’ and he said, ‘He is a thief and a violator of the dead.’”

key_terms.سَارِقٌ: a thief; one legally classified as having committed theft
key_terms.لِلْمَوْتَى: of the dead; referring to the sanctity of deceased persons
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَةَ: Mu'awiyah, during whose time this incident occurred
key_terms.نَبَّاشٌ: a grave-robber; one who exhumes graves unlawfully
key_terms.هَتَّاكٌ: a violator; one who desecrates sanctity
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: his hand is cut off; indicating the hadd punishment of amputation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a grave-robber in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling attributed to Imam Ali عليه السلام regarding the grave-robber. It presents grave robbery as a form of theft and violation of the sanctity of the dead, indicating that it falls under a severe penal category in jurisprudence.
